items.q: Chronic bronchitis is defined clinically by what?
o: Productive cough at least 3 months in each of 2 consecutive years
items.exp: Chronic bronchitis is a clinical definition (productive cough 3 months in 2 years) with mucous gland hypertrophy (Reid index), distinct from anatomical emphysema though both form COPD.
r: Incorrect. That defines emphysema anatomically.
Correct. The cough duration defines chronic bronchitis.
Incorrect. Reversible wheeze defines asthma.
Incorrect. Honeycombing defines fibrotic restriction.
items.kp: Bronchitis is a cough definition; emphysema is a tissue definition.

items.q: Early onset lower lobe panacinar emphysema in a non smoker suggests deficiency of what?
items.exp: Alpha 1 antitrypsin deficiency removes elastase protection, causing panacinar lower lobe emphysema early, plus liver disease from polymerised protein in hepatocytes (PiZZ).
r: Incorrect. Surfactant defects cause neonatal or fibrotic disease.
Correct. Antitrypsin deficiency causes panacinar emphysema.
Incorrect. CFTR causes bronchiectasis and pancreatic disease.
Incorrect. Elastin defects cause vascular and skin syndromes.
items.kp: Young basal emphysema: check alpha 1 antitrypsin and the liver.

items.q: Fatal asthma lungs characteristically show what?
o: Overinflation with widespread mucus plugging of airways
items.exp: Death in asthma follows asphyxia from mucus plugged, hyperinflated lungs with eosinophilic inflammation, Charcot Leyden crystals and thickened basement membranes. Air trapping prevents ventilation despite effort.
r: Incorrect. Granulomas suggest tuberculosis or sarcoid.
Correct. Plugged overinflated lungs kill in asthma.
Incorrect. Haemorrhage follows vasculitis or anticoagulation issues.
Incorrect. Plaques follow asbestos exposure.
items.kp: Fatal asthma is a plugging disease: mucus blocks every airway.

items.q: Usual interstitial pneumonia pattern fibrosis predominates where?
items.exp: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis scars subpleural basal lung with honeycombing and fibroblast foci, sparing upper zones relatively. Sarcoidosis instead favours upper lobes and hila.
r: Incorrect. Upper predominance suggests sarcoid or hypersensitivity patterns.
Correct. Basal subpleural honeycombing means UIP pattern.
Incorrect. Butterfly shadowing is pulmonary oedema.
Incorrect. Pleural disease alone is not interstitial fibrosis.
items.kp: Base plus subpleural plus honeycomb equals UIP fibrosis.

items.q: Plexiform lesions in small pulmonary arteries indicate what?
items.exp: Plexiform lesions are tufted capillary proliferations marking advanced irreversible pulmonary arterial hypertension, with medial hypertrophy and intimal fibrosis raising resistance to right ventricular failure.
r: Incorrect. Emboli are intraluminal clots, not wall plexiform change.
Correct. Plexiform change means severe arterial hypertension.
Incorrect. Venular disease obstructs post capillary vessels differently.
Incorrect. Ageing does not produce plexiform lesions.
items.kp: Plexiform equals severe fixed pulmonary arterial hypertension.

items.q: Pink puffer versus blue bloater contrast: the blue bloater tendency links mainly to what?
o: Chronic bronchitis dominance with hypoxia, CO2 retention and cor pulmonale
items.exp: Bronchitis dominant patients retain carbon dioxide, stay hypoxic and develop pulmonary hypertension with oedema (blue bloater), while emphysema dominant patients hyperventilate keeping gases near normal (pink puffer). Most patients mix both.
r: Incorrect. That describes the pink puffer pattern.
Correct. Bronchitis dominance bloats blue with cor pulmonale.
Incorrect. Asthma is episodic and reversible by definition.
Incorrect. Fibrosis restricts rather than obstructs gases this way.
items.kp: Blue bloater equals bronchitis, retained CO2 and right heart strain.

items.q: Bronchiectasis with chronic purulent sputum and finger clubbing most classically complicates which childhood disease?
items.exp: Cystic fibrosis thickens secretions through CFTR failure, causing chronic infection, bronchiectasis (upper lobe predominant), pancreatic insufficiency and clubbing from childhood.
r: Incorrect. Asthma rarely bronchiectases without allergic fungal disease.
Correct. Cystic fibrosis is the classic cause.
Incorrect. Antitrypsin deficiency causes emphysema, not suppurative airways.
Incorrect. Sarcoid restricts without purulent bronchiectasis.
items.kp: Childhood bronchiectasis plus pancreas failure equals cystic fibrosis.

items.q: Cor pulmonale means right ventricular failure secondary to what?
o: Lung disease or pulmonary vascular disease raising afterload
Mitral stenosis alone without lung change
items.exp: Cor pulmonale is right ventricular hypertrophy and failure from pulmonary hypertension caused by lung or pulmonary vascular disease, excluding left heart causes by definition.
r: Incorrect. Left failure causing right failure is not cor pulmonale strictly.
Correct. Lung driven pulmonary hypertension causes cor pulmonale.
Incorrect. Post capillary left heart causes are excluded from the term.
Incorrect. Systemic pressure loads the left ventricle.
items.kp: Cor pulmonale: lungs load the right heart to failure.

items.q: Reid index in chronic bronchitis measures what?
o: Mucous gland layer proportion of bronchial wall thickness
items.exp: The Reid index is mucous gland thickness divided by bronchial wall thickness, raised above about 0.5 in chronic bronchitis reflecting gland hypertrophy behind mucus hypersecretion.
r: Incorrect. Alveolar walls thin in emphysema instead.
Correct. Raised Reid index means gland hypertrophy.
Incorrect. Muscle hypertrophy characterises asthma airways.
Incorrect. Cartilage changes are not the Reid measurement.
items.kp: Reid index quantifies the mucus glands of bronchitis.

items.q: Which physiology pattern fits interstitial fibrosis?
o: Raised residual volume with low FEV1/FVC
Reduced total lung capacity with preserved or high FEV1/FVC and low transfer factor
Normal volumes with low transfer only in asthma
Raised total capacity with high transfer
items.exp: Fibrosis shrinks all volumes (low TLC) while flow ratio stays normal or rises because recoil increases, and transfer factor falls from membrane and capillary loss. Obstruction does the opposite.
r: Incorrect. That pattern is obstructive trapping.
Correct. Small stiff lungs with low transfer mean restriction.
Incorrect. Asthma transfer is usually preserved or high.
Incorrect. No fibrotic lung raises capacity and transfer.
items.kp: Restriction: small volumes, preserved ratio, low transfer.
